article.headline: Zscaler Jumps 19% Premarket On CrowdStrike's $43.9 Billion Stock Deal
article.deck: Friday's close sat 42.2% below the 337.09 buy point of a 53-week deep cup, and even the premarket price is far short of it; the deal, not the chart, now sets the stock.
body: Zscaler traded at 231.92 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, up 37.10, or 19.0%, after CrowdStrike agreed to acquire the cloud security company in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, as MT Newswires and Yahoo Finance reported Monday morning. The jump comes off a weak Friday, when the stock fell 10.89, or 5.3%, to 194.82 and traded 1.3x its 50-day average volume.

The chart is a 53-week deep cup, 66.0% from top to bottom, with a rim set Nov. 3, 2025 and a low of 114.62 on April 10. The buy point is 337.09, with a buy range up to 353.94. Friday's close sat 42.2% below the buy point, and the premarket price is also below the 298.48 52-week high.

Friday's close was 8.3% under the 50-day line at 212.42 and 5.5% under the 21-day line at 206.23; the session's range touched the 21-day line, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from it. The premarket price sits back above both lines. The stock is 16.8% above its 200-day line at 166.73. RS rank is 75 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 35.8% below its high. Shares were down 13.4% this year and 33.2% over twelve months through Friday.

Revenue in the quarter ended July 31 rose 24.9% to $898.2 million, the fourth straight quarterly rise from $788.1 million in the October 2025 quarter. The company lost 2 cents a share, after losses of 9 cents, 21 cents and 7 cents in the three quarters before. Market cap stood at $31.8 billion on a forward P/E of 34.59. The desk's calendar lists the next earnings report for Nov. 23.

A Stocktwits headline said JPMorgan sees the acquisition broadening CrowdStrike's security platform, with analysts weighing opportunities and risks. With an all-stock deal, Zscaler's price now moves with CrowdStrike's.
article.watch: Whether Zscaler holds above its 50-day line at 212.42 once the regular session opens.

article.headline: CrowdStrike Falls 8% Premarket After Agreeing To Buy Zscaler For $43.9 Billion
article.deck: Friday's close sat 20.1% below the 287.09 buy point of a seven-week cup, and the premarket price is under the base's 213.22 low.
body: CrowdStrike traded at 210.88 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 18.56, or 8.1%, after it agreed to acquire Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, as MT Newswires and Yahoo Finance reported Monday morning. Investor's Business Daily's live coverage headline said CrowdStrike plunged on the deal. The premarket drop follows a Friday loss of 14.02, or 5.8%, to 229.44, on volume 1.31x the 50-day average.

The stock is in a seven-week cup, 25.7% deep, with a rim set Oct. 6 and a low of 213.22 on Nov. 5. The buy point is 287.09, with a buy range up to 301.44. Friday's close sat 20.1% below the buy point. The premarket price is under the cup's low; a regular-session close there would undercut the base.

Friday's close was 2.6% under the 21-day line at 235.49 and 7.1% under the 50-day line at 247.04; the session's range touched the 21-day line, 0.0 ATRs from it. The stock is 30.2% above its 200-day line at 176.19 and 20.1% below its 286.99 52-week high. RS rank is 99 of 99 on the desk's list, with the RS line 6.9% below its high. Shares were up 95.8% this year and 76.3% over twelve months through Friday.

Revenue in the quarter ended July 31 rose 25.8% to $1.47 billion, up from $1.23 billion, $1.31 billion and $1.39 billion in the three quarters before. Earnings were 1 cent a share, after 3 cents, 4 cents and a 4-cent loss going back. Market cap stood at $234.9 billion on a forward P/E of 142.28. The desk's calendar lists the next earnings report for Nov. 23.
A Stocktwits headline said JPMorgan sees the deal broadening CrowdStrike's security platform, with analysts weighing opportunities and risks.

article.headline: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Rises 7% Premarket As Chip Stocks Lead Bounce
article.deck: Not buyable: Friday's close sat 44.5% below the 73.66 buy point of a six-week deep cup, at the bottom of the base.
body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise traded at 43.77 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, up 2.86, or 7.0%, as Barron's reported chip stocks leading a premarket bounce and MT Newswires reported futures rising as Nvidia started the week strong. On Friday the stock fell 4.58, or 10.1%, to 40.91, just above the 40.48 low it set that day, and traded 1.15x its 50-day average volume.

The chart is a six-week deep cup, 45.0% deep, with a rim set Oct. 9 and the low printed Friday. The buy point is 73.66, with a buy range up to 77.34. Friday's close sat 44.5% below the buy point and 44.4% below the 73.56 52-week high.

The close was 18.0% under the 21-day line at 49.91 and 29.1% under the 50-day line at 57.66. Friday's high stayed under the 21-day line, 1.44 ATRs from the 21-day line. The close was 4.2% under the 200-day line at 42.71; the premarket price is back above it. RS rank is 94 of 99 on the desk's list, with the RS line 37.0% below its high. Shares were up 70.3% this year and 98.6% over twelve months through Friday.

Earnings in the quarter ended July 31 rose 404.8% to $1.06 a share on revenue up 33.7% to $12.21 billion. Quarterly EPS has climbed from 11 cents to 31 cents, 44 cents and $1.06. Market cap stood at $54.3 billion on a forward P/E of 8.58. The desk's calendar lists the next earnings report for Nov. 23.

A TIKR headline said Dell and Super Micro want up to 45% more for AI servers already under contract, with Dell reporting Tuesday. A new base would have to form before the chart offers a buy point within reach.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds above its 200-day line at 42.71 in the regular session.
